subproblem.title: The support of a current equal to m[[M]] on an open set G lies, inside G, in the closure of M
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, G, M ⊆ ℝ^P be sets, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), m ∈ ℤ and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n). Assume G is open, G ⊆ U, and T(ω) = m·∫_M ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) (Hⁿ := μHE[n]) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω ⊆ G. Then spt T ∩ G ⊆ closure(M), where spt T = T.support = U ∖ zeroRegion T (Simon 6.2.11).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U G M : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (m : ℤ) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), IsOpen G → G ⊆ U → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ G → T ω = m * ∫ x in M, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μHE[n]) → T.support ∩ G ⊆ closure M
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the supplied proof of the selected node ("spt T ∩ B_ρ(y) ⊆ M": a point that has a ball missing M lies in the zero region, because every test form supported in that ball vanishes on M). Here it is stated for an arbitrary open set G ⊆ U on which T = m[[M]], with conclusion closure(M). No submanifold, orientation or measure hypothesis is needed. The selected node applies it with G = B_{ρ₀}(y), and then uses local compactness of M near y to replace closure(M) by M.
Conventions. Hⁿ := μHE[n]. For a current T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and a set W, "T vanishes on W" (T.VanishesOn W) means T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. zeroRegion T is the union of all open sets W with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and T vanishing on W, and spt T = T.support = U ∖ zeroRegion T (SimonGMT Chapter06/CurrentLocalEquality.lean; Simon 6.2.11).
1. Let x ∈ spt T ∩ G. Then x ∈ U, x ∉ zeroRegion T and x ∈ G. Suppose, for a contradiction, that x ∉ closure(M).
2. (A ball missing M.) The set G ∩ (ℝ^P ∖ closure(M)) is open, as the intersection of the open set G with the complement of the closed set closure(M), and it contains x. Hence there is ε > 0 with B_ε(x) ⊆ G and B_ε(x) ∩ closure(M) = ∅. In particular no point of M lies in B_ε(x).
3. (The set W.) Put W := B_{ε/2}(x). Then W is open and x ∈ W. Moreover closure(W) ⊆ closedBall(x, ε/2) (closure_ball_subset_closedBall). The closed ball is compact because ℝ^P is a proper metric space, so its closed subset closure(W) is compact. Finally closure(W) ⊆ closedBall(x, ε/2) ⊆ B_ε(x) ⊆ G ⊆ U, since ε/2 < ε.
4. (T vanishes on W.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Since W ⊆ B_ε(x) ⊆ G, the hypothesis gives T(ω) = m·∫_M ξ(z)(ω(z)) dHⁿ(z). Let z ∈ M. By step 2, z ∉ B_ε(x), so z ∉ W ⊇ tsupport ω. Hence ω(z) = 0, since a function vanishes outside its topological support (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). Then ξ(z)(ω(z)) = ξ(z)(0) = 0 because ξ(z) is linear. So the integrand vanishes at every point of M, and ∫_M ξ(z)(ω(z)) dHⁿ(z) = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero, which needs no measurability). Therefore T(ω) = m·0 = 0.
5. (Conclusion.) By steps 3 and 4, W is one of the sets whose union is zeroRegion T, and x ∈ W. Hence x ∈ zeroRegion T, contradicting step 1. Therefore x ∈ closure(M). Since x ∈ spt T ∩ G was arbitrary, spt T ∩ G ⊆ closure(M). ∎

```lean
theorem Submission.idtp_ccd_rps_support_subset_closure : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U G M : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (m : ℤ) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), IsOpen G → G ⊆ U → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ G → T ω = m * ∫ x in M, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μHE[n]) → T.support ∩ G ⊆ closure M := by
  intro P n U G M T m ξ hG hGU hrep x hx
  obtain ⟨hxT, hxG⟩ := hx
  by_contra hxcl
  obtain ⟨ε, hε, hball⟩ :=
    Metric.isOpen_iff.1 (hG.inter isClosed_closure.isOpen_compl) x ⟨hxG, hxcl⟩
  have hhalf : ball x (ε / 2) ⊆ ball x ε := ball_subset_ball (by linarith)
  have hclo : closure (ball x (ε / 2)) ⊆ ball x ε :=
    closure_ball_subset_closedBall.trans (closedBall_subset_ball (by linarith))
  apply hxT.2
  refine Set.mem_sUnion.2 ⟨ball x (ε / 2), ⟨isOpen_ball, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩, mem_ball_self (by linarith)⟩
  · exact (isCompact_closedBall x (ε / 2)).of_isClosed_subset isClosed_closure
      closure_ball_subset_closedBall
  · exact hclo.trans fun z hz => hGU (hball hz).1
  · intro ω hω
    rw [hrep ω (hω.trans (hhalf.trans fun z hz => (hball hz).1))]
    have h0 : ∫ z in M, ξ z ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) z) ∂μHE[n] = 0 := by
      apply setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero
      intro z hzM
      have hz : z ∉ tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) := fun hzt =>
        (hball (hhalf (hω hzt))).2 (subset_closure hzM)
      rw [image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport hz, map_zero]
    rw [h0, mul_zero]
```
proof_key_steps: A point x ∈ spt T ∩ G outside closure(M) has a ball B_ε(x) ⊆ G that misses M, because G ∖ closure(M) is open.
W := B_{ε/2}(x) is open, and its closure is compact and contained in B_ε(x) ⊆ G ⊆ U.
Every test form supported in W vanishes at each point of M, so T(ω) = m·∫_M ξ(z)(0) dHⁿ = 0. Hence x ∈ W ⊆ zeroRegion T, which contradicts x ∈ spt T.

subproblem.title: Points of an oriented C¹ submanifold M with T = m[[M]] (m ≠ 0) on an open set G lie in spt T
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, G, M ⊆ ℝ^P be sets, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), m ∈ ℤ and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n). Assume: G is open and G ⊆ U; m ≠ 0; M is an embedded C¹ n-dimensional submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 n M); ξ is an orientation of M (IsOrientation n M ξ: ξ is continuous on M, and for every z ∈ M, ξ(z) is a unit orientation of the subspace tangentSpace M z); Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ G (Hⁿ := μHE[n]); and T(ω) = m·∫_M ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω ⊆ G. Then M ∩ G ⊆ spt T, where spt T = T.support = U ∖ zeroRegion T (Simon 6.2.11).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U G M : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (m : ℤ) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), IsOpen G → G ⊆ U → m ≠ 0 → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 n M → IsOrientation n M ξ → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ G → μHE[n] (M ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ G → T ω = m * ∫ x in M, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μHE[n]) → M ∩ G ⊆ T.support
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the supplied proof of the selected node (M ∩ B_ρ(y) ⊆ spt T, the bump-form argument (a)–(g)). Here it is stated for an arbitrary open set G ⊆ U on which T = m[[M]], with both B_ρ(y) and B_{ρ₀}(y) of the supplied proof replaced by G. The supplied proof takes some facts from its steps 2–3; here they are obtained as follows. M is Borel by the sibling embedded_locally_closed. Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for the compact ball K ⊆ G is a hypothesis. The integrand is integrable because it is bounded by ‖α‖ on a set of finite measure, so compactness of M ∩ K is not needed.
Conventions. Hⁿ := μHE[n], ω_n := unitBallVolume n, B_r(x) := ball x r. For T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), "T vanishes on W" means T(ω) = 0 for each ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. zeroRegion T is the union of the open sets W with closure(W) compact and closure(W) ⊆ U on which T vanishes, and spt T = T.support = U ∖ zeroRegion T (Simon 6.2.11). Λⁿ = Covector (Euclid P) n carries the operator norm of continuous alternating maps, and Λ_n = MultiVector P n = (Λⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ) its operator norm, so |ξ(z)(β)| ≤ ‖ξ(z)‖·‖β‖.
0. (Facts about M and ξ.)
 (i) By the sibling embedded_locally_closed (Submission.dimred_rpd_embedded_locally_closed with r = 1, d = n), M is a measurable set.
 (ii) By IsOrientation n M ξ, ξ is continuous on M, and for every z ∈ M there is a subspace Q_z with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(z)) Q_z. So by the sibling unit_orientation_bounds (Submission.imsupp_unit_orientation_ne_zero_norm_le_one), ξ(z) ≠ 0 and ‖ξ(z)‖ ≤ 1 for every z ∈ M.
1. (Setting up the contradiction.) Let x ∈ M ∩ G. Then x ∈ U because G ⊆ U, so it remains to show x ∉ zeroRegion T. Suppose instead that x ∈ zeroRegion T. Then x ∈ W for some open set W (with closure(W) compact and contained in U) on which T vanishes.
2. (A covector α with ξ(x)(α) = 1.) By step 0(ii), ξ(x) ≠ 0, so there is α₀ ∈ Λⁿ with ξ(x)(α₀) ≠ 0; otherwise ξ(x) would be the zero functional. Put α := ξ(x)(α₀)⁻¹·α₀. By linearity, ξ(x)(α) = ξ(x)(α₀)⁻¹·ξ(x)(α₀) = 1.
3. (Continuity.) The function z ↦ ξ(z)(α) is continuous on M: ξ is continuous on M, and evaluating a continuous linear map at the fixed covector α is continuous (ContinuousOn.clm_apply with a constant). Since ξ(x)(α) = 1, there is ε₁ > 0 such that |ξ(z)(α) − 1| < 1/2, hence ξ(z)(α) > 1/2, for every z ∈ M with |z − x| < ε₁.
4. (Radius.) W ∩ G is open and contains x, so there is r > 0 with B_r(x) ⊆ W ∩ G. Put ε := min(r, ε₁) > 0. Then ε ≤ ε₁ and closedBall(x, ε/2) ⊆ B_ε(x) ⊆ B_r(x) ⊆ W ∩ G.
5. (The bump form.) Let g be Mathlib's smooth bump function centred at x with inner radius ε/4 and outer radius ε/2 (a ContDiffBump x with rIn = ε/4 and rOut = ε/2; note 0 < ε/4 < ε/2). It has these properties:
 - g is C^∞ and 0 ≤ g ≤ 1;
 - g = 1 on closedBall(x, ε/4) (one_of_mem_closedBall);
 - tsupport g = closedBall(x, ε/2) (tsupport_eq), so g(z) = 0 for z ∉ closedBall(x, ε/2);
 - g has compact support.
 Define the n-form ω(z) := g(z)·α. It is C^∞ as the product of the smooth function g and the constant α. It has compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right), and tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport g = closedBall(x, ε/2) (tsupport_smul_subset_left). Since closedBall(x, ε/2) ⊆ W ∩ G ⊆ U, we get ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), i.e. ω is a TestFormOn U n.
6. (T(ω) = 0.) tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(x, ε/2) ⊆ W and T vanishes on W, so T(ω) = 0.
7. (T(ω) as an integral.) tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(x, ε/2) ⊆ G, so the representation hypothesis gives T(ω) = m·∫_M h dHⁿ with h(z) := ξ(z)(ω(z)). By linearity of ξ(z), h(z) = ξ(z)(g(z)·α) = g(z)·ξ(z)(α).
8. (Properties of h.) Let μ := Hⁿ⌞M (μHE[n].restrict M) and K := closedBall(x, ε/2).
 (a) h is continuous on M, as the product of the continuous g and the function of step 3. Since M is measurable (step 0(i)), h is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable).
 (b) h(z) = 0 for z ∉ K, because g(z) = 0 there.
 (c) For z ∈ M, |h(z)| = |g(z)|·|ξ(z)(α)| ≤ 1·‖ξ(z)‖·‖α‖ ≤ ‖α‖, using 0 ≤ g ≤ 1 and step 0(ii). Since μ-almost every point lies in M, |h| ≤ ‖α‖ μ-a.e.
 (d) K is compact and K ⊆ G, so Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ by hypothesis. Since K is measurable, μ(K) = Hⁿ(K ∩ M) < ∞.
 (e) (Integrability.) By (a), (c) and (d), h is integrable on K with respect to μ, being a bounded a.e.-strongly measurable function on a set of finite measure (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded). By (b), h vanishes off K, so h is μ-integrable (IntegrableOn.integrable_of_forall_notMem_eq_zero).
 (f) (Nonnegativity.) h ≥ 0 μ-a.e. Let z ∈ M. If z ∈ K, then |z − x| ≤ ε/2 < ε ≤ ε₁, so ξ(z)(α) > 1/2 > 0 by step 3; with g(z) ≥ 0 this gives h(z) ≥ 0. If z ∉ K, then h(z) = 0 by (b).
 (g) (Where h is positive.) Let z ∈ M ∩ B_{ε/4}(x). Then z ∈ closedBall(x, ε/4), so g(z) = 1. Also |z − x| < ε/4 < ε₁, so h(z) = ξ(z)(α) > 1/2 > 0. Hence M ∩ B_{ε/4}(x) ⊆ {h ≠ 0} ∩ M.
9. (M has positive measure near x.) We claim Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{ε/4}(x)) > 0. Suppose instead that Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{ε/4}(x)) = 0. For every s ∈ (0, ε/4), monotonicity gives Hⁿ(M ∩ B_s(x)) = 0, so Hⁿ(M ∩ B_s(x))/(ω_n sⁿ) = 0, since in [0, ∞] zero divided by anything is zero. So this ratio is eventually 0 as s ↓ 0, and it tends to 0. But M is an embedded C¹ n-submanifold and x ∈ M, so by the sibling submanifold_density_one (Submission.dimred_rpd_submanifold_density_one) the same ratio tends to 1 as s ↓ 0. The filter s ↓ 0 (𝓝[>] 0) is nontrivial and limits in [0, ∞] are unique, so 1 = 0, which is absurd.
10. (The integral is positive.) For a μ-integrable function that is ≥ 0 μ-a.e., ∫ h dμ > 0 if and only if μ({h ≠ 0}) > 0 (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg_ae, applicable by 8(e) and 8(f)). By 8(g), step 9 and Measure.le_restrict_apply, μ({h ≠ 0}) ≥ Hⁿ({h ≠ 0} ∩ M) ≥ Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{ε/4}(x)) > 0. Hence ∫_M h dHⁿ = ∫ h dμ > 0. This is the supplied proof's bound ∫_M h dHⁿ ≥ ∫_{M ∩ B_{ε/4}(x)} h dHⁿ ≥ ½·Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{ε/4}(x)) > 0, stated as a positivity criterion.
11. (Contradiction.) By steps 6 and 7, 0 = T(ω) = m·∫_M h dHⁿ. But m ≠ 0, so (m : ℝ) ≠ 0, and ∫_M h dHⁿ > 0 by step 10, so the product is nonzero. This contradiction shows x ∉ zeroRegion T, hence x ∈ U ∖ zeroRegion T = spt T. Since x ∈ M ∩ G was arbitrary, M ∩ G ⊆ spt T. ∎

proof_key_steps: M is Borel (embedded_locally_closed), and ξ(z) ≠ 0 with ‖ξ(z)‖ ≤ 1 on M (unit_orientation_bounds). Pick α with ξ(x)(α) = 1, and ε₁ > 0 with ξ(z)(α) > 1/2 on M ∩ B_{ε₁}(x), by continuity of ξ on M.

If x ∈ zeroRegion T through an open W, take ε ≤ ε₁ with B_ε(x) ⊆ W ∩ G. The bump form ω = g·α, with g = 1 on closedBall(x, ε/4) and tsupport g = closedBall(x, ε/2), is a test form supported in W, so T(ω) = 0.
T(ω) = m·∫_M g·ξ(α) dHⁿ. The integrand is bounded by ‖α‖, measurable on M, vanishes off closedBall(x, ε/2), which has finite Hⁿ⌞M measure, is ≥ 0 on M, and is > 1/2 on M ∩ B_{ε/4}(x).
Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{ε/4}(x)) > 0 because the density ratio of M at x tends to 1 (submanifold_density_one). So ∫_M g·ξ(α) dHⁿ > 0 and T(ω) ≠ 0, since m ≠ 0, a contradiction. Hence x ∈ spt T.
